description: You can follow type-variable replacements through structures and chains.

steps.description: TVar names a type variable, TCon a fixed type, TFun a function type and TList a list type. You can nest these records to describe larger types.
apply follows variable bindings recursively and visits function and list components. compose applies its second-stage substitution to earlier bindings, while free_vars collects variable names.
You map α0 to Int and α1 to Bool. Applying that substitution changes (α0 -> α1) into (Int -> Bool).

steps.answer: It follows both bindings and returns Int, the fixed type at the end of the chain.
steps.question: Where does apply stop when α0 maps to α1 and α1 maps to Int?

steps.description: The chain test prints Int. You then compose the two single-binding substitutions and see both α0 and α1 mapped to Int.

title: Applying type substitutions
